insights.claim: The trainer operator implements dual gang-scheduler support (CoScheduling and Volcano) through separate runtime plugins, enabling deployment flexibility without compile-time scheduler selection.
insights.reasoning: Both CoScheduling and Volcano plugins implement the same runtime interface and create their respective PodGroup CRDs (scheduling/v1alpha1 vs scheduling/v1beta1). Runtime configuration determines which plugin is active, allowing operators to choose based on available cluster infrastructure.

insights.claim: RHOAI-specific extensions (progression monitoring, per-TrainJob NetworkPolicy) are isolated in pkg/rhai/ and gated by distribution-specific manifests, maintaining clean separation from upstream Kubeflow code.
insights.reasoning: The pkg/rhai/ package namespace contains RHOAI-only logic including NetworkPolicy CRUD per TrainJob and Pod-based progression tracking. These features are not present in upstream Kubeflow and are enabled through RHOAI-specific kustomize overlays and feature gates.

insights.claim: The TLS configuration dynamically adapts to the OpenShift cluster TLS security profile, providing centralized cipher suite management across webhook, metrics, and status servers.
insights.reasoning: Rather than hardcoding TLS settings, the operator reads config.openshift.io/v1/apiservers at startup and maps the cluster's TLS profile (Intermediate, Modern, Old, Custom) to Go crypto/tls configuration. This ensures the operator's TLS posture stays synchronized with cluster-wide security policy without manual per-component configuration.
